standards.name: Biological Collections Ontology (BCO)
standards.abstract: BCO is an ontology for describing biological collection objects and sampling processes. It is used to represent research objects such as museum specimens, environmental/metagenomic samples, and ecological survey observations; the primary recordings are semantic/ontology artifacts (OWL classes and properties) that model material samples, processes that create or observe them, and metadata about those entities. The standard (BCO) is maintained by the Biodiversity Ontologies/ Biocode Commons community and distributed via the OBO Foundry (purl.obolibrary.org). It addresses the problem of inconsistent and inadequate terminology for biodiversity sampling and specimen metadata, providing a shared set of classes and relations (and contribution/citation guidelines) to improve interoperability across museum collections, sequencing projects, and ecological datasets.

classification.rationale: The source material consists mainly of ontology files plus descriptive README and contribution guidance (prose and numbered guidelines). It does not present a row/column metadata table nor a directed sequence of ordered stages; instead it provides conceptual guidance and governance rules, so the best fit is PRINCIPLE (prose guidance and checklist-like contribution rules).

principles.principle: BCO supports interoperability of biodiversity and related data, covering museum collections, environmental/metagenomic samples, and ecological surveys.
principles.evidence: The BCO supports the interoperability of biodiversity and biodiversity related data, including data on museum collections, environmental/metagenomic samples, and ecological surveys. A key aspect of the BCO is distinguishing among material samples (i.e. specimens), observing processes, and data about either of those entities.

principles.principle: BCO distinguishes among material samples (specimens), observing processes, and data about those entities.
principles.evidence: A key aspect of the BCO is distinguishing among material samples (i.e. specimens), observing processes, and data about either of those entities.

principles.principle: BCO covers distinctions between individuals, organisms, voucher specimens, lots, samples, their relations, and sampling/usage processes; it also models properties such as collector, location, time, storage environment, containers, institution, and collection identifiers.
principles.evidence: The BCO covers distinctions between individuals, organisms, voucher specimens, lots, samples, the relations between these entities, and the processes governing the creation and use of "samples". Also within scope are properties including collector, location, time, storage environment, containers, institution, and collection identifiers.

principles.principle: BCO is part of the OBO Foundry and aims to conform to OBO Foundry principles.
principles.evidence: The Biological Collections Ontology (BCO) is part of the OBO Foundry library and attempts to conform to [OBO Foundry Principles](http://www.obofoundry.org/principles/fp-000-summary.html)

principles.principle: Community contribution process: join the mailing list and use the issue tracker for new term requests or changes.
principles.evidence:
Join the BCO Google Groups mailing list at bco-discuss@googlegroups.com. You can browse the list at https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!forum/bco-discuss.

New terms requests or changes to the ontology should be made using our [issue tracker](https://github.com/BiodiversityOntologies/bco/issues)

principles.principle: Guidelines for contribution: provide detailed requests, examples/references, suggested label/definition/hierarchy for new terms, and detailed rationale for relationship updates.
principles.evidence:
1. **Write a detailed request:** Please be specific and include as many details as necessary, providing background information, and if possible, suggesting a solution. GOC editors will be better equipped to address your suggestions if you offer details regarding *'what is wrong'*, *'why'*, and *'how to fix it'*. 

2. **Provide examples and references:** Please include DOIs or PMIDs for new term requests, and include also screenshots, or URLs illustrating the current ontology structure for other types of requests. 

3. **For new term request:** Be sure to provide suggestions for label (name), definition, references, position in hierarchy, etc. 

4. **For updates to relationships:** Provide details of the current axioms, why you think they are wrong or not sufficient, and what exactly should be added or removed.

standards.name: Observations and Measurements (OGC/ISO 19156)
standards.abstract: This standard defines a conceptual model for observations and measurements of geographic phenomena: observations evaluate properties (phenomena) of features under particular contexts (location, time, sampling) and produce results expressed as measurements, classifications, coverages or other result types. The document is an OGC Abstract Specification (Topic 20) produced jointly with ISO (ISO 19156) and provides a schema-level model (UML and conceptual classes such as OM_Observation, OM_Process/Procedure, ObservationContext, NamedValue and SamplingFeature), guidance on packaging and use, and classifications of specialised observation types and result forms. It is intended to provide a common, interoperable model for encoding and exchanging observation/measurement information across geospatial systems.

classification.rationale: The source is a prose specification and conceptual model (UML classes and explanatory sections). It defines model elements and guidance rather than presenting a row/column field table or a sequential process. The document is structured as descriptive sections and normative prose (definitions, schema descriptions and classifications), matching the 'principle' category.

standards.name: Information Artifact Ontology (IAO) — annotation properties (excerpt)
standards.abstract: This source is an OWL/XML excerpt from an ontology file (ontology_metadata_bco_imports.owl) that defines annotation properties used to describe ontology terms and metadata in OBO/OWL artefacts. The research object is metadata about ontology classes and properties (information artifacts) represented in RDF/OWL; the modality is an ontology file (XML serialization of OWL) containing annotation property declarations, labels, and prose definitions. The material is part of the Information Artifact Ontology (IAO) as used within OBO Foundry/OBI contexts; it documents annotation properties (e.g., editor preferred term, definition, example of usage) that standardize how ontology terms are named, defined, and curated. The excerpt appears to be maintained by the IAO/OBO ecosystem (authors named include Daniel Schober, Alan Ruttenberg, Bill Bug, Melanie Courtot) and addresses the problem of providing standardized annotation properties and human-readable metadata for ontology development and curation.

classification.rationale: The source is prose/XML declaring a set of annotation properties each with labels and human-readable definitions. It is not a table of named data fields with explicit data types, nor does it describe an ordered sequence of procedural steps; therefore it best maps to a set of 'principles' (named metadata annotation properties with descriptions) rather than a table or DAG.
